incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287 through 287-43 governing Yuhan Hoesa limited liability companies; Article 3 (notarization of articles of incorporation) and Article 24 (establishment registration). For non-resident investments, Framework Act on Foreign Investment and its Enforcement Decree apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's principal office; for filings in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, supported by KOTRA one-stop incorporation services for foreign investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), filed with the District Court Registration Office together with notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of paid-in capital deposit, members' register, and consents of directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed by the Korean Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa; the Articles may state a fixed capital amount, and every subscription must be fully paid in cash or kind into the Company's domestic bank account before establishment registration. No statutory blocked escrow account requirement applies. Registration taxes and fees are assessed proportionately on declared capital; if foreign investment notification is made, remittance of the investment amount into the domestic bank account must be completed in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act or KOTRA report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE DIRECTORS OF KR YUHANGHOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) (the 'Company'), adopted by unanimous written consent of all directors effective on the date of incorporation. WHEREAS the Company is organized as a Yuhan Hoesa under Articles 287 through 287-43 of the Korean Commercial Act; and WHEREAS the founding members have subscribed in full to the initial capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation; and WHEREAS the directors deem it necessary to complete statutory registration, establish banking authority, adopt a registered office, and appoint statutory officers. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. The initial capital amount expressly set forth in Article 4 of the Articles of Incorporation, namely Korean Won [CAPITAL], is hereby ratified and accepted as fully subscribed by the founding members. The directors shall ensure that each member's contribution is paid in full into the deposit account designated for the Company and that the certificate of capital payment is attached to the establishment registration application. Each member shall be recorded in the register of members with the amount and class of capital contribution. No founder's shares, options, or other rights in addition to the subscribed capital are granted. 2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The principal office address shown in Article 2 of the Articles of Incorporation is adopted as the registered office and statutory seat of the Company for service of process, tax domicile, and corporate governance purposes. The representative director is instructed to execute the office lease, obtain the building owner's use consent, and promptly notify the competent District Court Registration Office and the National Tax Service of any future relocation. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Company shall maintain its primary transaction and settlement accounts with a bank licensed under the Banking Act of the Republic of Korea. The representative director and one other director are jointly authorized to open such accounts, to designate specimen signatures, and to approve all domestic and international fund transfers, including SWIFT wire transfers and documentary letters of credit required for used construction excavator and roller remaketing transactions. Any disbursement above the internal threshold shall require dual approval under the Company's two-man control rule. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The following persons are appointed to the offices stated, each to serve until resignation or removal pursuant to the Articles: [NAME] as Representative Director, [NAME] as Director and Chief Financial Officer, and [NAME] as Auditor if required by law or the Articles. The Representative Director shall represent the Company before courts, registries, tax offices, and industrial licensing authorities and shall cause this resolution to be filed with all competent government agencies. 5. DELEGATION AND FILING. The Representative Director and Chief Financial Officer are jointly and severally authorized to execute the establishment registration, business registration, used machinery trading permits, banking documentation and all ancillary filings and to retain qualified Korean legal counsel for such purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) and a Korean Notary Public appointed under the Notary Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator shall first search the corporate-name database of the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office to confirm that the proposed Korean name and the English transliteration YUHANGHOESA are not identical or confusingly similar to any pre-existing registered entity. After the name is reserved or approved, the incorporator shall prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing the precise corporate name, business purpose covering wholesale remaketing of secondhand hydraulic earthmovers and rollers, registered office address, declared capital amount, total number of capital contributions, contribution value per member, representation clause, and term if any. All founding members must subscribe the articles by signature or seal, and the articles must then be notarized by a Korean notary public. The notarized articles constitute the foundational governance instrument; no subsequent amendment is effective until approved at a members' meeting and, if required, registered.
required_dossiers: Name search result or availability printout
Passport or national ID cards of all founding members
Power of attorney if signed by an agent
Proof of registered office address or preliminary lease consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected because of identity or similarity with an existing company, the incorporator shall immediately file a revised name search and amend the articles. If the notary raises a defect in the purpose clause or contribution provisions, the incorporator shall correct the articles and re-execute subscriptions. Any delay caused by overseas notarization can be cured by using a consular-legalized power of attorney and overnight courier service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: HomeTax System (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) in South Korea, the entity must obtain a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) from the local district tax office (세무서) under the jurisdiction of its registered address. The application is submitted via the HomeTax System or in person, with the following documents: articles of incorporation, certificate of foreign investment (if applicable), lease agreement for the registered office, and identification of the representative. After approval, the NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number (사업자등록번호) which serves as the VAT ID and corporate tax ID. For non-resident entities without a local permanent establishment, a simplified VAT registration may be required if they make taxable supplies in Korea. The process typically takes 3-5 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is automatically treated as a domestic corporation for Korean tax purposes; no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are available for this entity type.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No threshold; any business with taxable supplies must register for VAT. However, a simplified taxpayer regime applies to small businesses with annual revenue below KRW 48 million (for wholesale/retail) or KRW 80 million (for services), which reduces compliance burden but does not exempt registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-invoices) must be issued for all B2B transactions via the HomeTax System. E-invoices must be transmitted to the NTS by the 10th of the following month. There is no real-time fiscal clearance, but the NTS uses a digital e-invoice system for cross-matching and anti-fraud analytics. Additionally, cash receipts must be issued for consumer transactions, and a fiscal receipt device is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Article 21 of the VAT Act. To claim zero-rating, the exporter must prove that the goods were physically exported from Korea and that the export proceeds are received in foreign currency. For used construction machinery, the exporter must provide evidence of the export declaration and the actual shipment. Services directly connected to exported goods may also qualify for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export zero-rating is claimed without proper documentation or if the export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, the NTS will assess VAT at 10% on the export value, plus an additional tax of 40% of the VAT as a penalty. In cases of fraud, criminal penalties may apply, including fines up to KRW 100 million and imprisonment. The NTS conducts post-export audits and may claw back any refunds previously granted.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Customs Service, under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and regulations promulgated by the Foreign Exchange Administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade payments, service fees, royalties, and dividend remittances, subject to submission of underlying evidence to a licensed foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions, including direct equity investments, foreign borrowing, and cross-border loans, operate under a declaration-and-registration rather than a blanket prohibition, but require filing under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and, for foreign direct investment, reporting under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. A foreign investor injecting equity into a Korean limited liability company must open a temporary Foreign Currency Deposit Account with a domestic Korean bank, deposit the inward remittance, convert it into Korean won, and complete a post-investment capital verification process before the funds can be used. Profit remittance is permitted after corporate tax returns and withholding tax settlement, with the bank requiring certified financial statements, tax payment certificates, board-approved dividend resolution, and tax treaty residence confirmation to support the outward remittance. Because Korea maintains a free-floating regime but restricts speculative non-trade capital flows, all large wire transfers require explicit FX purpose codes, and the bank will reject remittances lacking a clearly documented underlying transaction. The practical hurdle for a used heavy machinery wholesaler is not convertibility itself but the evidentiary burden of proving asset valuation and the commercial reality of cross-border trades with countries posing sanctions-related or trade-based money laundering risks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Korea does not impose a mandatory surrender-to-central-bank ratio or a forced KRW conversion percentage. Exporters must repatriate and settle export proceeds in foreign currency through a licensed foreign exchange bank within six months from the date of the export declaration, either by converting to KRW or by retaining the funds in an approved Foreign Currency Deposit Account. If payment is legitimately delayed by buyer default or documentary discrepancies, the exporter must apply for an extension through the settlement bank before the six-month deadline lapses. The applicable statutory principle is full repatriation and settlement, with 0% forced conversion, but 100% of export receipts must be reportable and traceable through the Korea Customs Service export declaration and bank settlement records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW/USD Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Exchange Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail. Offshore fintech EMI platforms cannot service this entity as a principal account bank because they do not hold a Korean banking license and are legally barred from accepting KRW deposits, issuing local IBAN-like settlement accounts, or performing foreign investment capital verification under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. They may be used only as ancillary payment aggregators that settle through a licensed Korean bank, never as the receiving institution for FDI capital injections, export proceeds repatriation, or statutory capital verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorized director or a formally appointed senior officer must appear in-branch for identity verification, banking authorization signature, and e-banking issuance. Remote consular proxy opening is possible in limited cases if the board resolution and power of attorney are notarized and apostilled, with the consulate confirming the representative's passport, but the majority of Korean banks still require a physical compliance interview for foreign entities, especially when entering foreign exchange, escrow, and trade finance facilities. The final decision rests with the bank's foreign exchange compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity arising from multi-layer non-resident shareholding in the Korean LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from the Korean registry, complete shareholders register showing direct and indirect ownership to natural persons, notarized personal passport copies of all UBOs, bank reference letters from the originating banks, source-of-wealth statements supported by tax returns, corporate financial statements, and audited business operating histories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag triggered by subjective valuation of secondhand construction excavators and possible over- or under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent pre-shipment inspection and valuation report from a recognized equipment appraiser such as SGS, Bureau Veritas, or KOMA-accredited machinery assessor; equipment serial number and manufacture year verification from the Korea Construction Machinery Safety Center; original purchase invoices, repair and maintenance logs, photograph and telematics history, export customs declaration, and a documented floor-price reconciliation model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use or sanctions concern where used hydraulic excavators may be diverted to prohibited end-users or military infrastructure projects in high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user certificate and end-use declaration signed by the ultimate customer, re-export prohibitions in the sales contract, fully declared logistics chain and Bill of Lading, sanctions and denied-party screening reports for all counterparties, corporate-ownership transparency certificates, and confirmation that the machinery will not enter North Korea, Russia, Iran, Syria, or other comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident capital source mismatch: inbound FDI funds originate from a third-party jurisdiction or the remitting entity differs from the registered foreign investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Report acknowledgement from MOEF or the receiving bank, SWIFT MT103 covering an amount exactly matching the equity subscription agreement, a statement from the applicant's home-country bank confirming the ultimate financial source, twelve months of pre-funding bank statements, an executed capital contribution resolution, tax residence certificates for all funding shareholders, and a written explanation of the exact economic purpose of the capital injection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must first file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or a licensed foreign exchange bank, then remit the equity contribution via SWIFT MT103 to the Korean bank's Foreign Currency Deposit Account established in the name of the Korean entity or the foreign investor. The remittance must clearly identify the investor, the target entity, and the foreign exchange purpose code for equity acquisition or capital increase; after receipt, the bank converts the foreign currency to KRW at the market rate into a temporary capital escrow account, verifies the paid-in capital, and issues the foreign investment certificate. Capital verification is completed by comparing the subscribed capital in the notarized articles of incorporation, the bank credit advice, and the balance on the escrow account, after which funds are released to the operating account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imports of used excavators and spare parts, the preferred rails are SWIFT MT103 for open-account settlements, commercial letters of credit issued through the Korean bank's trade finance desk for high-value confirmed goods, and documentary collections D/P or D/A for goods financed under conditions where an LC is not commercially justified. All outbound trade payments must be matched against the Korea Customs Service import declaration, the commercial invoice, packing list, Bill of Lading, and inspection certificate, with the bank applying the appropriate foreign exchange trade purpose code. Export sale proceeds from overseas buyers of heavy machinery must also be collected by SWIFT MT103 through the Korean bank within the six-month statutory export settlement period, and the bank will monitor trade finance exposure against the underlying trade documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts (KRW/USD, KRW/JPY, KRW/EUR) for hedging underlying trade receivables and payables, with maturity aligned to the settlement date of the equipment transaction

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts executed through a licensed Korean bank to hedge KRW exposure when the offshore counterparty requires non-deliverable settlement, with the contract strictly capped at the notional amount of the underlying trade invoice or capital commitment

Cross-currency interest rate swaps for medium-term external borrowing or foreign-currency working capital facilities, subject to Foreign Exchange Transactions Act declaration and restrictions limiting the swap to hedging actual asset-liability mismatches rather than speculative trading

Currency options and exotic structures only when linked to defined trade settlement obligations and approved by the bank's treasury and compliance desk, with no permission for leveraged speculative derivatives absent a real underlying commercial exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (including annual financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies, by March 31 of the following year (a one-month extension is available with NTS approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; understatement penalty of 10% of the deficient amount; overdue tax accrues daily interest at 0.022% (approximately 8.03% per annum). Prolonged non-payment can trigger asset seizure, cancellation of business registration, and court-ordered administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surcharge (Seoul Metropolitan / Provincial Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Local Government (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government through the local tax collection office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the Corporate Income Tax Return; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, due by March 31 of the following year (with identical one-month extension option)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the local tax due; underreporting penalty of 10% of the underpaid amount; overdue interest at 0.022% per day. Repeated delinquency can lead to local tax seizure and potential administrative strike-off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly deadlines: Q1 (Jan-Mar) by April 25; Q2 (Apr-Jun) by July 25; Q3 (Jul-Sep) by October 25; Q4 (Oct-Dec) by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid VAT; understatement penalty of 10% of the deficient amount; overdue interest at 0.022% per day. Sustained non-compliance may prompt cancellation of the VAT business registration and enforcement seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report (when mandatory under the External Audit and Accounting Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART (Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System) and attached to the Corporate Income Tax Return filed with the NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending December 31, the audit report must be issued and filed with FSS/DART by March 31 of the following year; for other fiscal year ends, within 90 days after the year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or to submit the audit report may result in criminal fines up to KRW 50 million, imprisonment, civil liability for damages, and regulatory sanctions including suspension of business activities or administrative dissolution in severe cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Foreign Investment Enterprise (if the entity qualifies as a foreign-invested company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By February 15 of each calendar year for the preceding year's foreign investment status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing false information carries penalties under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act of up to KRW 2 million; may also lead to revocation of foreign-investment tax preferences and benefits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean External Audit and Accounting Act (Act No. 14817, effective 2018), a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company) is mandatorily required to undergo an independent external audit if, as of the immediately preceding fiscal year-end, its total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million). The audit requirement also applies regardless of asset size to listed companies, financial institutions (banking, insurance, securities, mutual-financing), and entities issuing public bonds. In addition, shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares may, with valid grounds, request an audit, and certain creditors may trigger an audit for asset-managed companies. The threshold is based on unconsolidated or consolidated total assets as determined by the applicable accounting framework.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Companies subject to statutory audit must prepare financial statements in accordance with K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards). Non-public companies below the K-IFRS mandatory application scope may elect K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or the SME Accounting Standards issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, provided they meet the eligibility conditions for small and medium-sized entities. All financial statements must be presented in the Korean language and currency (KRW).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not require an annual UBO (beneficial ownership) confirmation filing for a private limited liability company. Instead, the company must maintain an up-to-date register of members; any transfer of equity interests must be duly recorded in that register after approval of the general meeting of members. Under the Commercial Registration Act, any change in registered office, directors, or registered capital must be filed with the competent District Court Commercial Registry within 30 days of the change. For foreign-invested enterprises, any shareholding change or changes to foreign investor details must be reported to KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Furthermore, financial institutions are required by AML regulations to collect and validate beneficial ownership information at account opening and periodically; however, no general-purpose annual UBO return is submitted to a central register in Korea.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (General Meeting and Board Meeting minutes)
Accounting Books and Annual Financial Statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - 2,200 per year for standard registered office and local compliance agent services in Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - 35,000 per year for a company near or above the mandatory audit threshold; USD 7,000 - 15,000 for voluntary or limited-scope audits; USD 0 if fully exempt and no audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge (maximum combined 27.5% for taxable income above KRW 30 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones may claim a 3-5 year corporate tax holiday and a 50% reduction for the following 2 years under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; R&D expenditures qualify for a tax credit up to 30% under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; SMEs enjoy additional rate reductions and deferral privileges; no patent-box regime is currently implemented.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Form 1 and attached schedules) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; mandatory semi-annual prepayment (interim tax return) due by August 31
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide turnover reported on the cash or accrual basis as elected for tax recognition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate all used-excavator export consideration derived from foreign buyers; do not offset commission or freight costs against sales; reconcile with customs export declarations. A Korean resident company is taxable on worldwide sales; foreign-earned income is not automatically excluded, but treaty-based relief may apply only where a foreign permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary business expenses, including cost of goods sold, depreciation, bad debts, wages and foreign trade commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When importing used machines from related foreign vendors, deduct only arm's-length purchase price substantiated by customs valuation, inspection reports and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. Cross-border digital, telematics and software fees paid to nonresident entities are nondeductible unless withholding tax was actually withheld and paid to the Korean tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 20 - Tax-Exempt Income and Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income arising from certain dividends, treaty-exempt items and statutory reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exemptions claimed by the Korean entity require documentary proof of foreign income and the underlying foreign tax certificate; any foreign tax credit claimed must be supported by an official foreign tax receipt. Discounts or rebates from a foreign intra-group supplier cannot be treated as exempt income; they are a cost reduction or purchase-price adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base computed after combining gross income, deductible expenses, non-deductible items, loss carryforwards and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity has intercompany debt from a non-resident shareholder, apply Korea's thin-capitalization rules under Article 52 of the Corporate Tax Act; a debt-to-equity ratio above 3:1 disallows interest deductions, and the disallowed amount is recharacterized as a deemed dividend subject to 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 40 and Schedule 12 - Foreign Taxes and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income tax credit, including credit for taxes paid to treaty jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only foreign income tax legally payable on Korean-source or foreign-source income of the Korean resident company is creditable; foreign VAT is not creditable. Submit the foreign tax certificate and apply the foreign tax credit carryforward, which is allowed for up to five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 14 - Information Return on Payments to Nonresident and Foreign Corporations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of dividends, interest, royalties, service fees and other payments made to nonresident shareholders or foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must identify each nonresident recipient by name, residence jurisdiction, tax identification number and beneficial-ownership status. Failure to withhold and report triggers a maximum 40% additional tax on the under-withheld amount and the payment becomes nondeductible; the payer's officers may be personally liable under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 20% additional tax on the unpaid amount, plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% (capped at 36 months); negligent under-reporting: 10% additional tax; fraudulent under-reporting: 40% additional tax; failure to submit transfer-pricing documentation for an international transaction: 30% additional tax on the understated tax. Criminal tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 50 million under the Special Act on Aggravation of Punishment for Specific Economic Crimes.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge = 22% on gross dividends paid to a nonresident shareholder. Treaty rate reductions generally apply (commonly 5% for substantial shareholdings, 15% for portfolio dividends; US-Korea treaty 15% portfolio / 10% for 10% shareholders).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the nonresident payee must submit to the Korean paying entity before payment an application for exemption or reduction under the applicable treaty (HomeTax electronic Form 24), attach a Certificate of Tax Residence issued by the foreign competent authority, provide a duly signed beneficial-ownership declaration, and supply board resolutions or underlying contracts establishing the recipient's functional substance. If the application is incomplete or the beneficial ownership is challenged under the BEPS MLI minimum standard (LOBP/PPT), Korea will withhold at the statutory 22% rate and the foreign shareholder must file a refund claim through a local tax representative; refund resolution commonly takes six to twelve months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 22% (20% national plus 2% local surcharge); treaty rates commonly 10% (e.g., US-Korea treaty 10%) and in certain treaties 0% for bank interest. Royalties: statutory 22%; treaty rates commonly 10% for industrial royalties and 15% for copyright or cinematographic royalties under the US-Korea treaty; domestic law requires the payer to withhold and remit before remitting the gross payment, with criminal sanctions for non-withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 76 million) in gross revenue, or a cross-border related-party transaction volume of KRW 50 billion; a Local File is also mandatory when any intercompany transaction category exceeds KRW 5 billion, and a Master File is required for groups with consolidated revenue above KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies the economic-substance and substance-over-form doctrines under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 52 of the Corporate Tax Act. A company with no real office, no core income-generating activities in Korea, and with profits shifted to a low-tax offshore entity will be recharacterized and subjected to the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR). Although Korea does not apply OECD Economic Substance Regulations directly, the BEPS provisions and case law require functional and factual substance for both treaty benefits and intercompany pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-border tax evasion / willful omission of sales from used excavator exports
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting or omitting sales of used excavators sold through a foreign logistics depot or related offshore entity; booking cash proceeds in undisclosed foreign bank accounts; issuing side agreements that alter payment by SWIFT LC to untraceable cash without reporting to Korean customs or the National Tax Service.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 109(1) of the Corporate Tax Act imposes imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 50 million; Article 34(2) of the Framework Act on National Taxes adds a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty and 20% unfaithful-report penalty; overdue interest of 0.022% per day accrues on the unpaid tax, capped at 36 months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 39(1) of the Framework Act on National Taxes, a director who materially participated in the evasion is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax if corporate assets are insufficient; the Special Act on Aggravation of Punishment for Specific Economic Crimes raises the imprisonment term to 5 years and mandates travel-restriction (blacklisting), asset seizure and personal bank account freezing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent transfer pricing / abuse of a low-tax offshore intermediary
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling used construction equipment to a controlled Hong Kong, Singapore or UAE buying company at a non-arm's-length discount or purchasing through the intermediary at an inflated price with no business rationale; failing to prepare Local or Master File once the statutory threshold is exceeded; using a shell company with no employees, premises or risk-bearing capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 4(4) of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the National Tax Service adjusts the taxpayer to the arm's-length range and imposes an additional tax of 10% of the understated tax; if contemporaneous documentation is not submitted the penalty rises to 30%; a secondary adjustment applies, treating the difference as a deemed dividend subject to 22% withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or signed the defective pricing are personally liable for the adjusted tax and penalty; article 11 of the same law creates a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to KRW 20 million; Korean courts pierce the corporate veil when the entity is a mere façade, and the court may attach the director's personal overseas real estate and assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering failure on unreported cash and split payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving USD 50,000 or more in cash for used excavators from overseas buyers and deliberately failing to file a suspicious-transaction report with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit; structuring cash deposits in amounts under KRW 20 million to avoid the mandatory cash reporting threshold; maintaining a currency-exchange side ledger used for cross-border bribes or informal value transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 13(1) of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information punishes failure to report financial transactions with imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 30 million; if proceeds are criminal in nature, the Act on Confiscation and Regaining of Criminal Proceeds permits seizure of the company's assets and the proceeds of the machines; repeat offenders face up to 5 years of imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Article 14(2) of the AML Act imposes individual criminal liability on the responsible director unless he or she proves the transaction was concealed from management and unauthorized; directors involved in the structuring are subject to immediate travel bans, account freezes, permanent criminal records, disqualification from board service for regulated activities, and, if convicted of underlying bribery, forfeiture of personal assets and civil damages under the Korean Commercial Act and Foreign Bribery Prevention Act.
